issues.reason: "simple majority" is a named voting threshold, exactly the term-of-art trigger *Compound concepts* gives for fusing an adjective+noun into a recognized kind, so the split form applies the incidental-description treatment that rule reserves for colour/size/damage/mood and predicates simplicity of the majority, which the sentence does not state.

The occurrence-object carve-out is bounded to verbs that change whether or when the occurrence happens (cancel / call off / postpone / delay / reschedule / bring forward); "decide" settles a vote's outcome, not its happening, and *Thematic roles* directs "when the test is unclear, default to Theme", so Patient is the unlicensed marked choice.

new_gaps: a singular-indefinite subject with a verbal predicate stating a standing procedural rule ("A simple majority decides a vote") has no licensed generic carrier: *Existential* mandates the one-off witness reading because a verbal generic needs a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, so the standing-rule content the sentence actually conveys is unencodable
defect_summary: The compliant form fuses the term of art as (Member sk_majority_1 simple_majority) with the head genus (Inheritance simple_majority majority) — the modifier genus emitted or withheld by the usual predication test — instead of the two-atom split; and the direct object takes (Theme sk_decide_1 sk_vote_1) rather than Patient.
notes: The reviewer is right that the absent status atom (habitual default) and the plain witness for the singular collective "majority" are correct; the faults are confined to the fusion branch and the object role.
